title: Derived adjunction of inverse and direct image on D^+
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with the adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ on the abelian sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], the inverse image $u^{-1}:\Dplus(V_{\Et})\to\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ on bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and the derived direct image $Ru_*:\Dplus(U_{\Et})\to\Dplus(V_{\Et})$, $Ru_*K=u_*I(K)$ for a K-injective resolution $K\to I(K)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], on morphisms through the homotopy classes of the induced maps of resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Then $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$: there is an adjunction, with unit $\eta^D_u:\mathrm{id}\to Ru_*u^{-1}$ and counit $\varepsilon^D_u:u^{-1}Ru_*\to\mathrm{id}$, uniquely determined by the following two properties.
(1) For a bounded below K-injective complex $I$ of sheaves on $U_{\Et}$ (so that $u_*I$ represents $Ru_*I$), the counit $\varepsilon^D_{u,I}:u^{-1}u_*I\to I$ is the class in $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ of the morphism of complexes $(\varepsilon_{u,I^r})_r$.
(2) For a bounded below complex $M$ of sheaves on $V_{\Et}$ and a K-injective resolution $u^{-1}M\to J$, the unit $\eta^D_{u,M}:M\to Ru_*u^{-1}M=u_*J$ is the class of $M\xrightarrow{(\eta_{u,M^r})_r}u_*u^{-1}M\to u_*J$.
Equivalently, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dplus(U_{\Et})}(u^{-1}M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dplus(V_{\Et})}(M,Ru_*K)$ bifunctorially, by the bijection sending $a$ to $Ru_*(a)\circ\eta^D_{u,M}$.

source.place: Lemma 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors) and Lemma 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), with Lemma 015F for the exact left adjoint; for ringed topoi Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 07A6 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-adjoint), where the base change map of Remark 07A7 uses this adjunction

proof.text: (K-injectivity of the direct image.) The inverse image $u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\to\Ab(U_{\Et})$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and left adjoint to $u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; $u_*$ is additive, being a right adjoint between additive categories (it preserves finite products, hence biproducts). By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] (with $u=u_*$, $v=u^{-1}$), for every K-injective complex $I$ of abelian sheaves on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] the termwise complex $u_*I$ is a K-injective complex on $V_{\Et}$; if $I$ is bounded below, so is $u_*I$ (termwise, $u_*0=0$).

(The adjunction on homotopy categories.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to $v=u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]: for every complex $M$ of abelian sheaves on $V_{\Et}$ and every complex $I$ on $U_{\Et}$ the map

$$
 \alpha_{M,I}:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U_{\Et})}(u^{-1}M,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{K(V_{\Et})}(M,u_*I),\qquad[f]\mapsto[u_*(f)\circ\eta_{u,M}],
$$

$\eta_{u,M}=(\eta_{u,M^r})_r$, is bijective with inverse $[g]\mapsto[\varepsilon_{u,I}\circ u^{-1}(g)]$, $\varepsilon_{u,I}=(\varepsilon_{u,I^r})_r$, and natural in homotopy classes of maps $M'\to M$ and $I\to I'$.

source.place: Lemma 08BJ, proof (display 'By adjointness we get Hom_{K(A)}(v(M),I) = Hom_{K(B)}(M,u(I))')

proof.text: (Morphisms into K-injective complexes.) By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], for a complex $N$ and a K-injective complex $J$ of abelian sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ ($T=U$ or $V$) the localization functor gives a bijection $Q:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T_{\Et})}(N,J)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\Et})}(QN,QJ)$, natural in homotopy classes of maps $N'\to N$ and of maps $J\to J'$ between K-injective complexes (because $Q$ is a functor). Since $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ is a full subcategory of $D(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], morphisms between objects of $\Dplus$ are the same in $\Dplus$ and in $D$; below all Hom sets are taken in $D$.

(The two functors on representatives.) By [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], for every complex $M$ on $V_{\Et}$ there is an isomorphism $\varphi_M:u^{-1}(QM)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u^{-1}M)$ in $D(U_{\Et})$, natural in morphisms of complexes $M'\to M$ (here $u^{-1}$ on $D$ is the functor $u^{-1}_D$ of that node, whose restriction to $\Dplus$ is $u^{-1}$). By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], each $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ comes with its K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], i.e. a bounded below K-injective complex $I(K)$ and an isomorphism $\rho_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI(K)$ in $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ (the image of the resolution quasi-isomorphism, inverted by $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]); $Ru_*K=Q(u_*I(K))$, and for $a:K\to K'$, $Ru_*(a)=Q(u_*\tilde a)$, where $\tilde a:I(K)\to I(K')$ is the unique homotopy class with $Q(\tilde a)\circ\rho_K=\rho_{K'}\circ a$ (unique and existing by step 3, $I(K')$ being K-injective).

source.place: Lemma 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies): RF(I) = F(I) for K-injective I; Lemma 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text:
(The bijection.) For a complex $M$ on $V_{\Et}$ and $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ let $\Psi_{M,K}$ be the composite of the bijections

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}_D(u^{-1}QM,K)\xrightarrow{a\mapsto\rho_K a\varphi_M^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_D(Q(u^{-1}M),QI(K))\xleftarrow[\ \sim\ ]{Q}\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U_{\Et})}(u^{-1}M,I(K))\xrightarrow{\alpha_{M,I(K)}}\operatorname{Hom}_{K(V_{\Et})}(M,u_*I(K))\xrightarrow[\ \sim\ ]{Q}\operatorname{Hom}_D(QM,Q(u_*I(K)))=\operatorname{Hom}_D(QM,Ru_*K).
$$

The first map is bijective since $\rho_K$ and $\varphi_M$ are isomorphisms (step 4); the second by step 3, $I(K)$ being K-injective; the third by step 2; the fourth by step 3, $u_*I(K)$ being K-injective by step 1. So $\Psi_{M,K}$ is a bijection. (Stacks proves Lemma 0DVC through the colimit description of Lemma 0FND; with K-injective resolutions, which compute $Ru_*$ by Lemma 070K, the colimit over $K\to I$ is attained at $I(K)$ and that argument becomes this chain, which is the one of the proof of Lemma 08BJ.)

source.place: Lemma 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors, line 9570) and its general form Lemma 0FND (line 9515); Lemma 08BJ proof; Lemma 070I

proof.text: (Naturality in $K$.) Let $a:K\to K'$ in $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ with $\tilde a$ as in step 4. Each map of the chain of step 5 commutes with composition by $a$, resp. its image: the first because $\rho_{K'}a=Q(\tilde a)\rho_K$; the second because $Q$ is a functor; the third by the naturality of $\alpha$ in $I$ (step 2), $[f]\mapsto[\tilde a f]$ going to $[g]\mapsto[u_*(\tilde a)g]$; the fourth because $Q$ is a functor and $Ru_*(a)=Q(u_*\tilde a)$. Hence $\Psi_{M,K'}(a\circ b)=Ru_*(a)\circ\Psi_{M,K}(b)$ for all $b:u^{-1}QM\to K$.

source.place: Lemma 0DVC ('functorial in both variables'; Stacks omits the proof of functoriality)

proof.text: (Naturality in the first variable, and extension to all objects.) For a morphism of complexes $f:M'\to M$ on $V_{\Et}$, $\Psi_{M',K}(b\circ u^{-1}(Qf))=\Psi_{M,K}(b)\circ Qf$: $\varphi$ is natural in $f$ (step 4), $Q$ is a functor, and $\alpha$ is natural in $M$ (step 2). Fix $K$ and consider the functors $F'_1=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\Et})}(u^{-1}_D(-),K)$ and $F'_2=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\Et})}(-,Ru_*K)$ from $D(V_{\Et})$ to $\mathrm{Sets}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $F_i=F'_i\circ Q$ on complexes, which invert quasi-isomorphisms. Then $(\Psi_{M,K})_M:F_1\to F_2$ is a natural isomorphism, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) (with $\phi_i=\mathrm{id}$) there is a unique natural isomorphism $\Psi_{-,K}:F'_1\to F'_2$ with $\Psi_{QM,K}=\Psi_{M,K}$. For $a:K\to K'$ the two natural transformations $X\mapsto Ru_*(a)\circ\Psi_{X,K}(-)$ and $X\mapsto\Psi_{X,K'}(a\circ-)$ from $F'_1(K)$ to $F'_2(K')$ agree at every $X=QM$ by step 6, hence everywhere by part (3) of that node. Restricting to $X\in\Dplus(V_{\Et})$, where $u^{-1}_DX=u^{-1}X$ (step 4), gives bijections $\Psi_{X,K}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dplus(U_{\Et})}(u^{-1}X,K)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dplus(V_{\Et})}(X,Ru_*K)$ natural in both variables.

source.place: Lemma 0DVC (functoriality, omitted in Stacks); Categories, Lemma 04VG (universal property of the localization), as recorded in the cited node

proof.text: (The adjunction.) By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] applied to $F=u^{-1}$, $G=Ru_*$ and $\Psi$ (step 7), $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ is an adjunction with unit $\eta^D_{u,X}=\Psi_{X,u^{-1}X}(\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}X})$ and counit $\varepsilon^D_{u,K}=\Psi^{-1}_{Ru_*K,K}(\mathrm{id}_{Ru_*K})$, whose hom bijection is $\Psi$, i.e. $\Psi_{X,K}(a)=Ru_*(a)\circ\eta^D_{u,X}$: this is the last sentence of the statement.

source.place: Definition 0037 (definition-adjoint) and the paragraph after it

proof.text: (Property (1).) Let $I$ be a bounded below K-injective complex on $U_{\Et}$ and $K=QI$. By step 3 the isomorphism $\rho_K:QI\to QI(K)$ is $Q(h)$ for a unique homotopy class $h:I\to I(K)$, and $\rho_K^{-1}=Q(h')$ for a unique $h':I(K)\to I$; by the injectivity in step 3, $h'h=\mathrm{id}$ and $hh'=\mathrm{id}$ in the homotopy category, so $h$ is a homotopy equivalence and $Q(u_*h):Q(u_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u_*I(K))=Ru_*K$ is the identification under which '$u_*I$ represents $Ru_*I$'. Compute $\varepsilon^D_{u,K}=\Psi^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_{Ru_*K})$ with $M=u_*I(K)$ along the chain of step 5 backwards: $\mathrm{id}$ comes from $[\mathrm{id}_{u_*I(K)}]$, which $\alpha^{-1}$ sends to the termwise counit $[\varepsilon_{u,I(K)}]$ (step 2), so $\varepsilon^D_{u,K}=\rho_K^{-1}\circ Q(\varepsilon_{u,I(K)})\circ\varphi_{u_*I(K)}$. By naturality of the termwise counit, $\varepsilon_{u,I(K)}\circ u^{-1}u_*(h)=h\circ\varepsilon_{u,I}$; composing with $u^{-1}Q(u_*h)$ on the right (and using naturality of $\varphi$) gives $\varepsilon^D_{u,K}\circ u^{-1}(Q(u_*h))=Q(\varepsilon_{u,I})\circ\varphi_{u_*I}$. That is, under the identification $Ru_*I\cong Q(u_*I)$, the counit at $I$ is the class of the morphism of complexes $(\varepsilon_{u,I^r})_r$, which is (1).

source.place: Lemma 070I and Lemma 08BJ proof; the description of the counit is not stated in Stacks

proof.text: (Property (2).) Let $M$ be a bounded below complex on $V_{\Et}$, $X=QM$, $K=u^{-1}X$. By step 3, $\rho_K\circ\varphi_M^{-1}:Q(u^{-1}M)\to QI(K)$ is $Q(r)$ for a unique homotopy class $r:u^{-1}M\to I(K)$; $Q(r)$ is an isomorphism, so $r$ is a K-injective resolution of $u^{-1}M$. Computing $\eta^D_{u,X}=\Psi_{M,K}(\mathrm{id}_K)$ along step 5: $\mathrm{id}_K\mapsto\rho_K\varphi_M^{-1}=Q(r)\mapsto r\mapsto u_*(r)\circ\eta_{u,M}\mapsto Q(u_*(r)\circ\eta_{u,M})$. So $\eta^D_{u,M}$ is the class of $M\xrightarrow{\eta_{u,M}}u_*u^{-1}M\xrightarrow{u_*r}u_*J$ with $J=I(K)$. For any other K-injective resolution $r':u^{-1}M\to J'$, step 3 gives a unique homotopy class $c:J\to J'$ with $cr=r'$, a homotopy equivalence as in step 9, and $u_*(c)\circ u_*(r)\circ\eta_{u,M}=u_*(r')\circ\eta_{u,M}$; so (2) holds for every choice of $J$, compatibly with the identifications $Q(u_*c):Q(u_*J)\cong Q(u_*J')$.

source.place: Lemma 070I and Lemma 08BJ proof; the description of the unit is not stated in Stacks

proof.text: (Uniqueness.) Let $(\eta',\varepsilon')$ be any adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ on $\Dplus$. If $\varepsilon'$ satisfies (1), then for every $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$, by naturality along the isomorphism $\rho_K:K\to QI(K)$, $\varepsilon'_K=\rho_K^{-1}\circ\varepsilon'_{QI(K)}\circ u^{-1}Ru_*(\rho_K)$, and $\varepsilon'_{QI(K)}$ is prescribed by (1), $I(K)$ being bounded below and K-injective; so $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon^D_u$ (which satisfies (1) by step 9). If $\eta'$ satisfies (2), then $\eta'_{QM}=\eta^D_{u,QM}$ for every bounded below complex $M$ (step 10); every $X\in\Dplus(V_{\Et})$ is isomorphic to such a $QM$ (the objects of $D(V_{\Et})$ are the complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a complex with $\mathcal H^i=0$ for $i<n$ is quasi-isomorphic to its truncation $\tau_{\ge n}$, which is bounded below [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]), so by naturality $\eta'=\eta^D_u$. In either case [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-ext] gives $(\eta',\varepsilon')=(\eta^D_u,\varepsilon^D_u)$.

split_report.summary: Statement kept; 'morphism of schemes' repointed from def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions to def-pc-scheme, the sheaf categories cited (def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves) and Ru_* on morphisms cited (lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated). Proof in 11 steps: K-injectivity of u_*I (new lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective, Stacks 08BJ, unsplit), the termwise adjunction on homotopy categories (new lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy, unsplit), Hom into K-injectives computed in K (new lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived, Mathlib leaf IsKInjective.Qh_map_bijective / Plus.Qh_map_bijective_of_isKInjective, Stacks 070I), the bijection Hom(u^{-1}QM,K) = Hom(QM,Ru_*K) by the chain of 08BJ (in place of the ind/pro argument of 0DVC/0FND), naturality in both variables (localization universal property, existing leaf), the adjunction from the natural bijection (new leaf Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv), computation of counit (1) and unit (2) on representatives, uniqueness (new leaf Adjunction.ext / ext_counit). u^{-1} being its own derived functor (lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor) is not needed and not cited. Mathlib's Adjunction.localization does not apply (u_* does not descend). Proof marked agent: Stacks states 0DVC but not (1), (2) or uniqueness; KS 14.4 wanted.
